project.name: ts-employee-service
conventions: Handlers stay thin — query logic lives in `features/<domain>/helpers/*.service.ts` (static-method service classes); handlers orchestrate services and never call `db` directly.

Procedures are built from `publicProcedure`/`protectedProcedeure` in `packages/api/src/routers/router.base.ts` (keep the existing spelling), and each declares `.route({ method, path, summary })` plus an `.output(...)` Zod schema.
Errors are `ORPCError("UNAUTHORIZED" | "FORBIDDEN" | "NOT_FOUND" | "BAD_REQUEST", { message })` — never a bare `throw new Error` in a handler.
Reuse generated schemas from `@service/validators` instead of hand-writing shapes; regenerate after schema changes rather than editing generated files.

Schema changes go `packages/db/src/schema/*.schema.ts` -> `db:generate` -> review the SQL -> `db:migrate`. Never hand-edit `src/migrations/`, and never run `db:migrate-prod` without explicit per-command human approval.
Env vars are per-app (`apps/server/.env` via `packages/env`, `apps/web/.env` via `apps/web/src/env.ts`) — never consolidated into a root `.env`, and `.env*` secrets are never read or echoed.
Formatting is oxfmt's job — don't reflow unrelated code.
trustBoundaries: `authenticatedUser()` middleware reads the gateway-injected `userid` header into `context.userId` — never trust a caller-supplied identity beyond that header. Reading identity from a body, query param, or other header is a spoofing vector: flag it as critical.
`isHRStaff()` gates HR-only routes — verify every HR-only route actually applies it; a route copy-pasted from a public one is the most common way this gets missed.
`packages/api/src/myidtravel/` talks to an external partner API — treat its responses as untrusted input requiring validation, not as safe to pass through unchecked.
This service handles employee/HR personal data, so object-level authorization on employee/relative/travel-request IDs is the highest-value thing to audit.

angles.name: correctness
angles.covers: Does the change actually solve the stated problem, and what edge cases does it miss.
angles.triggeredBy: always — every non-trivial change gets this angle

angles.name: schema
angles.covers: Drizzle schema/migration implications and backward compatibility of existing rows.
angles.triggeredBy: the change touches `packages/db/src/schema/`, requires a migration, or changes a Drizzle field/table

angles.name: contract
angles.covers: Breaking changes for consumers of an oRPC procedure's `.route()`/`.input()`/`.output()` or an exported type.
angles.triggeredBy: the change touches a procedure signature or a type exported from `@service/api` / `@service/validators`

angles.name: auth
angles.covers: `authenticatedUser()`/`isHRStaff()` correctness and caller-supplied identity trust boundaries — check BOLA first.
angles.triggeredBy: the change touches auth middleware, permission gating, or any fetch-by-ID handler

angles.name: operability
angles.covers: Logging, error handling, observability, and `ORPCError` usage — how failures get diagnosed in production.
angles.triggeredBy: the change affects error paths, logging, or external-call failure handling

domains.match: visual layout as part of the ticket
a small viewport or touch interaction
auth, user input validation, or an external integration

signals: adds or changes a Drizzle schema field non-destructively
changes internal service logic used by multiple callers
changes or removes a Drizzle column/table
changes an existing oRPC procedure's `.output()` signature
changes a type exported from `@service/api` or `@service/validators`

lessons: A subagent once mutated a pre-existing branch because its self-report was trusted without checking `git diff` — verify every step's diff yourself before moving on.

On #111/PR #171 a reviewer note about a `previousData` type was "fixed" in a follow-up commit pushed without re-running `check-types`, so the real mismatch shipped to CI instead of being caught locally. Re-run the actual check after every fixup.

Tool restrictions declared in an agent's frontmatter are a stated intent, not an enforced boundary here — an agent without Edit/Write declared was still able to modify a file. That is why the `Agent:` git trailer is mandatory regardless of declared tool scope.

web.apiClient: generated via `openapi-ts` into `src/lib/api/client/` — regenerate with `bun --filter web gen:api`, never hand-edit generated files
